brief: Zero Hedge argues a costlier bond market is pushing hyperscaler AI capex off balance sheet into special purpose vehicles, and that resulting circularity is growing. Demand for Amazon's long-dated bonds weakened at its July $25bn sale versus March's upsized $50bn one, so Amazon is reportedly moving about $8bn of Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips into an SPV, selling up to 10% of its equity and leasing the chips back for an investment-grade rating off its AA credit, even as AWS raises GPU rental prices about 15%. Separately, Broadcom's bank syndicate is raising $60bn, split into a $42bn senior tranche and an $18bn Blackstone-led junior tranche, to finance Anthropic's purchase of Broadcom chips, with Broadcom backstopping the senior notes. The circle: Amazon has committed up to $83bn to Anthropic, which leases AWS compute and Broadcom chips. Blackstone is both lender and Anthropic investor. Nvidia is reportedly in talks to anchor Anthropic's IPO. Goldman's Privorotsky calls this standard evolution but says circularity is undeniably increasing. The document's own view: this converts operating risk into credit risk, the dynamic that stalled Oracle's SPV-funded Project Jupiter without demand collapsing, only growth decelerating.
